descriptions.text: Buta-1,3-diene is a butadiene with unsaturation at positions 1 and 3. It has a role as a mutagen and a carcinogenic agent.

1,3-Butadiene can cause cancer according to an independent committee of scientific and health experts. It can cause developmental toxicity, female reproductive toxicity and male reproductive toxicity according to The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) and The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
descriptions.source: California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment (OEHHA)

uses: 1,3-Butadiene is used in the production of rubber and plastics. It is also used in copolymers including acrylics.

Used in the production of synthetic rubber for motor vehicle tires; also used in styrene-butadiene polymers, acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene resins, and other compounds; [ACGIH] In a study of Swedish refinery workers, The exposure to 1,3-butadiene among all exposure groups was low (95% of all samples were below 10 ug/m3) in relation to the Swedish OEL, of 1000 ug/m3. id.title: 1,3-Butadiena
id.extract: 1,3-Butadiena adalah diena terkonjugasi dengan rumus kimia C4H6. Senyawa ini merupakan senyawa industri penting yang digunakan sebagai monomer dalam produksi karet sintetis. Ketika istilah butadiena digunakan, kebanyakan senyawa yang dimaksud adalah 1,3-butadiena.

en.title: Butadiene
en.extract:
1,3-Butadiene ( ) is an organic compound with the formula CH2=CH−CH=CH2. It is a colorless gas that is easily condensed to a liquid. It is important industrially as a precursor to synthetic rubber. The molecule can be viewed as the union of two vinyl groups. It is the simplest conjugated diene.
Butadiene undergoes chemical degradation in the atmosphere, but it can nevertheless be found in low levels in the air of urban and suburban areas due to emission by motor vehicles.
The name butadiene can also refer to the isomer, 1,2-butadiene, which is an allene (a cumulated diene) with structure H2C=C=CH−CH3 that has no industrial importance.
